conviction_note: The evidence points to a miss against the stale Bloomberg consensus of ARS 219.5bn: the BCRA's domestic-private-bank group, BBAR, SUPV and GGAL all printed Q3 far below Q2 and below their own estimates. But the market saw all of that before this print (BMA -7.65% in 5 days, -17% in 20 days, at its 52-week low, at about half the sell-side targets), management's FY guide already implied a weaker second half, and a buyback is buying daily. So the findings net to -0.4 and p_up sits only 6 points under 50 on an abs move of 4.0. The 2027 guide comes on the 11-30 call, outside the window.

BCRA's September data show NPLs and default probability falling, so the credit lines are unlikely to be cut. Guidance is normally given on the call, which is on 2026-11-30 after the exit window, so the window most likely sees the numbers without a new guide.

findings.finding: BCRA's Informe sobre Bancos for September 2026, published 2026-11-20, puts system Q3 ROA at 0.8% annualised (ROE 3.4%), against a Q2 ROA of 2.5% in its June report. The domestic private bank group ('EFB priv. nac.', which includes Macro) shows a 3-month ROA falling from about 1.4% in July to about 0.5% in September (Chart 17). The BCRA blames a lower 'margen financiero integral', partly offset by lower loan-loss charges, which fell as irregular loans dropped to 7.50% (families 12.20%, down 0.61pp). This is a broad series that contains Macro's own quarter and points to a peso miss against the Bloomberg consensus of ARS 219.5bn, which sits above Macro's Q2 206.8bn.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: a 31.5% EPS beat traded -1.6% after hours. Q4 2025: profit 39% below the Bloomberg consensus (Bloomberg Linea, 'Banco Macro vuelve al verde pero no alcanza estimaciones'); that reaction was not sourced. On 2026-11-24 GGAL fell about 1% on a roughly 12% consensus miss.
findings.why_not_priced: The consensus is visibly above Q2 (219.5 against 206.8bn) and has not been rebuilt on this series. If the market had fully priced it, the sell-side numbers would have converged down; Citi's 188.5bn and Goldman's -19% predate the 11-20 BCRA release. Part of it is priced anyway: BMA fell 7.65% in the 5 sessions spanning the BCRA release and the peer prints.
findings.independence: Peer prints from separate issuer documents point the same way: BBAR's 6-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000913059/000129281426005393/bbarpr3q26_6k.htm), SUPV (https://www.riotimesonline.com/grupo-supervielle-q3-earnings-2026/) and GGAL (https://www.rava.com/noticias?ticker=GGAL_US). The BCRA aggregate contains those banks, so this finding and the peer findings share a common driver and are sized with that overlap in mind. Macro has the group's highest capital (CET1 28.4% per Goldman), and less leverage means less ROE sensitivity to margin.
findings.link: Macro is one of the banks inside the 'EFB privados nacionales' group the series aggregates.

findings.finding: BBVA Argentina's 3Q26 6-K (2026-11-24) reports inflation-adjusted net income of AR$58.9bn, -57.7% QoQ, with ROE 4.9% against 12.2%, total NIM 15.1% against 18.2%, and fair-value income on government securities AR$16.4bn against 34.2bn. Citi had estimated AR$124.5bn, 6% below a Bloomberg consensus near 132bn (iProfesional 2026-11-13), so BBAR missed by more than half, and Goldman's ROE forecast of 8.8%. The CFO expects 'an upward path in profits' from Q4.
findings.link: Both are large private Argentine universal banks under the same BCRA rate and reserve-requirement regime, with large peso government-securities books. Goldman forecasts Macro's NIM falling 17.6% to 16.3%, a smaller drop than BBAR's 18.2% to 15.1%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: BBAR's own reaction on 2026-11-25 was not found. BMA has not paid for reported-quarter beats (Q2 2026 -1.6% on a 31% beat).
findings.why_not_priced: The BMA estimates were set on 2026-11-13, before this print, so the BMA consensus has not absorbed the size of BBAR's margin and securities shortfall. Because the BBAR release is public, much of it is already in BMA's 5-day -7.65%.
findings.independence: The BCRA September report is a separate document on the same driver (margin compression). SUPV's NIM fell 20.3% to 16.0% (https://www.riotimesonline.com/grupo-supervielle-q3-earnings-2026/).

findings.finding: Grupo Financiero Galicia reported 3Q26 net income of ARS 229.0bn on 2026-11-24, down 16% QoQ on a smaller financial margin, with NPLs down to 9.7%. Citi had forecast 272.5bn, 5% above the Bloomberg consensus (about 259.5bn), so GGAL missed consensus by about 12%. Its ADR fell more than 1%.
findings.link: The largest private domestic bank, in the same rate and reserve regime and the same BCRA group as Macro. Goldman forecast GGAL recurring profit -15% QoQ against -19% for Macro, so the actual -16% was in line with Goldman and below Citi and Bloomberg.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: GGAL ADR fell more than 1% on the miss, 'in line with other Argentine banks' (Bloomberg Linea via Rava). This peer's market punished a consensus miss only mildly.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: a public print one day before Macro's. It supports a miss against the Bloomberg consensus, which was built before the peer prints, and it also shows how small the reaction to a consensus miss was (-1%). That damping is why it is sized small.
findings.independence: BCRA series (separate document); the BBAR 6-K. The Galicia figures come from press summaries aggregated on Rava (Forbes Argentina, Bloomberg Linea, iProfesional), not from the GFG press release itself.

findings.finding: Grupo Supervielle's 3Q26 attributable net income was AR$6.8bn (2.2% ROE; AR$10.7bn excluding severance), half of Q2's 13.6bn. NIM fell 20.3% to 16.0% and net financial income fell 22.4%. Citi had forecast AR$28.3bn, 15% below a consensus near 33bn, so SUPV missed by about 75%.
findings.link: Smaller private domestic bank in the same rate regime. It is more retail and consumer-credit heavy than Macro and has a much thinner capital base (CET1 13.5% against Macro's 28.4%), so the read-through on margin is partial.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: SUPV's stock reaction on 2026-11-16/17 was not found.
findings.why_not_priced: Public since 2026-11-16, before the Citi and Goldman previews were widely circulated (13 Nov) and before the BCRA release. It mostly confirms the system-wide margin squeeze, which BMA's 20-day -17% already reflects.
findings.independence: Same driver as the BBAR and BCRA findings, so it is sized smallest of the three peers.

The headline consensus is stale against the two broker previews.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 2025: profit 39% below the Bloomberg consensus (Bloomberg Linea); that reaction was not sourced. Q2 2026: a beat traded -1.6%.
findings.why_not_priced: Headline screens will show a miss against 219.5bn. The buy-side reading the Citi and Goldman notes expects less, which is why this is capped small: the bar is disputed between sources (Chartmill implies about 200bn).

findings.finding: On 2026-08-19 management guided FY2026 reported ROE to 9-10% (adjusted about 12%) after Q1 at 10% and Q2 at 13.4%. That arithmetic implies a second-half ROE of roughly 7-8%, about ARS 110-130bn a quarter on an equity base near ARS 6.2tn (inferred from Q2's 206.8bn at 13.4%). A Q3 well below the Bloomberg 219.5bn would therefore sit inside what the company itself guided.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide changes on the Q2 call (loans cut to 2-5% from 15-20%, ROE guide raised) came with a -1.6% after-hours reaction and a slide from $75 to $50 since.
findings.why_not_priced: A consensus of 219.5bn is visibly inconsistent with the company's own 9-10% reported ROE guide. Had the street priced the guide, the consensus would sit near 130-170bn and a 'miss' headline would not be in prospect. The equity base and the H2 split are this hunter's arithmetic on a transcript summary, not a company figure, hence the small size.
findings.independence: Goldman's ROE 11.2% forecast sits between the guide-implied rate and consensus (iProfesional 2026-11-13).

findings.finding: Expectations are already low. BMA trades at $49.79, its 52-week low, 52% below the 52-week high, -17.3% over 20 days and -7.65% over 5 days. That is about 49% of the $100.71 Bloomberg consensus target and below every cut target (UBS $90 on 10-19, Goldman $95 on 11-13). Citi and Goldman both name Macro their only buy among Argentine banks. The 5-day fall covered the SUPV, BCRA, GGAL and BBAR releases, so a sector-wide Q3 miss is substantially in the price.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Peer GGAL fell only about 1% on its 12% consensus miss on 11-24, the day after a similar de-rating.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself: what is priced is a sector margin miss. The finding says the bar the ADR holds is below the headline consensus, so a print near the broker numbers can hold or lift the stock. If the market were not braced, BMA would not have fallen 7.65% across the peer-print week.
findings.independence: Sealed baseline tape (run-up fields); Goldman target cut on 2026-11-13 (https://www.iprofesional.com/finanzas/468851-wall-street-recomienda-una-sola-accion-entre-los-bancos-argentinos).

findings.finding: Banco Macro's board approved a buyback on 2026-10-28 of up to 20M Class B shares (Ps.160bn cap, max Ps.10,700, 45 calendar days, so it runs to about mid-December). It has bought on most sessions since 2026-10-30: 503,318 shares on 10-30, 294,214 on 11-11, 536,223 and 737,916 in the week of 11-17, 78,138 on 11-20, and 430,000 disclosed 11-24. Panabee tallies about 3.0M shares for Ps.28.6bn through 11-24, under 20% of the cap. The cap is about US$100m at about 1,600 ARS/USD, roughly 3% of market capitalisation, and it can keep buying through the window.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No precedent on the reaction found. BMA has kept falling while the buyback ran (about -21% since 10-19).
findings.why_not_priced: The program is public, but its remaining capacity (over 80% unspent) is a live bid into a thin post-Thanksgiving half-day. Buenos Aires trades Thursday 11-26 while New York is shut, and the buyback can absorb local selling that would otherwise arbitrage into the ADR on Friday. Had it been fully priced, the stock would not be at a fresh 52-week low.
findings.independence: Execution disclosures via https://www.panabee.com/news/macro-bank-repurchases-294-thousand-shares-for-ps-2-8-billion (2026-11-24) and the Rava BMA news feed (https://www.rava.com/noticias?page=1&ticker=BMA).

findings.finding: Inside the quarter-close window, on 2026-10-28, about four weeks after Q3 closed and with the quarter's numbers largely in hand, Macro's board stated that the share price 'does not adequately reflect the value of its assets or its capacity to generate results' and committed up to Ps.160bn of capital. No other mid-quarter operating statement was found.
findings.why_not_priced: Boards rarely spend excess capital on buybacks just before a disastrous quarter they already know about, so the act is weak evidence against a BBAR-style collapse. The stock's continued fall shows the market has not read it that way. Sized small because it is an inference from behaviour, not a figure.
findings.independence: Shares one corporate act with the buyback finding (capital), which counts the bid. This finding counts only the information content, and the sizes are kept apart and small for that reason.

findings.finding: Citi raised its local target for Macro to ARS 15,500 from 9,680 (buy) while forecasting a below-consensus Q3. Both picked Macro as the one bank to own into the prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Wire-level and largely priced. The sell-side owns a below-consensus Q3 and stays positive, so a miss against Bloomberg is less likely to trigger downgrades in the window.
findings.independence: Shares a document with the consensus_bar finding; the two read different lines (the bar against the stance).

findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 beat sold -1.6%; the baseline's 8 'moves' are buyback 6-Ks, not prints, and were not used.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a reaction function, not a fact the price lacks. It caps the upside of a beat and is filed so the judges can weigh it.
findings.independence: GGAL's muted -1% on a miss (Rava, 2026-11-24) suggests the sector's print reactions are damped both ways and that macro drives these ADRs.

On 2026-08-19 management said it needs 'at least one more quarter' before giving 2027 loan guidance, so the 2027 guide (loan growth, ROE, any dividend or buyback renewal) most likely arrives on that call, after the exit window closes on 2026-11-27. baseline_tension: The fundamental evidence (BCRA aggregate and three peer misses) points to a miss against the Bloomberg consensus and agrees with the -17% 20-day run-up. That agreement means it is largely priced, and with no usable skew and a small, non-crowded short there is nothing to fight. The net lean is slightly negative and p_up is held near 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (bar verification): the consensus has one Bloomberg figure and a Chartmill figure about 10% lower, so it is disputed. The consensus_bar finding was capped from -0.4 to -0.2 and the bar-dependent peer findings were trimmed (BBAR -0.8 to -0.6, GGAL -0.4 to -0.3, SUPV -0.3 to -0.2). print_vs_bar moved from -25 to -20.

Lesson 6 and the core table (inside guidance): a miss against consensus would land inside the company's own FY reported-ROE guide of 9-10%. The BCRA finding was shrunk from -1.2 to -1.0 and p_up moved toward 50.
Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction; the name sold its Q2 beat) plus the pessimism-artefact note: p_up moved from 42 to 44. The reaction_history finding stays at -0.2.
Lesson 5 (broad series beats narrow proxy): left the BCRA aggregate as the largest negative and the individual peers below it. No change beyond the above.

Lessons on untrustworthy FPI history: the 6-K 'reaction' base rate was not used. abs_move_pct was rebuilt from confirmed prints and 20-day realised volatility (38% annualised, about 3.4% over two sessions) and set at 4.0 rather than 4.5, still above the realised-volatility scale as the core requires.
Lessons 7 and 8 (positioning, thin coverage): short interest is checked and not crowded, so no change.
